tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local claim/idempotency fixture. A provider terminal proof P_I5 is immutably bound to logical operation O5, payload digest D5, and provider idempotency identity I5; it is complete for all I5 attempts, permanently sealed/quiescent for I5, and explicitly attests no irreversible effect for I5. A later authoritative repository claim keeps O5 and D5 but rotates the provider idempotency identity to I6 under a fresh current fence F7. Test only whether P_I5 can by itself support repository terminal negative closure for the I6 claim. No concrete provider, public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler state, hosted compute, richer-mode arbitration, finite quota, or second semantic leaf is tested.

premises: P_I5 is exact-domain evidence for O5,D5,I5 only.
P_I5 proves complete I5 attempt history, permanent I5 sealing/quiescence, and explicit no-effect for every I5 attempt.
The later repository claim preserves O5 and D5 but changes provider idempotency identity from I5 to I6.
No premise states that I6 is provider-equivalent to I5, inherits I5 sealing, or is incapable of creating a distinct provider attempt namespace.
Repository finalization under F7 still requires current-claim CAS and exact readback.
fixture.candidate_action: Reuse P_I5 as the sole provider-side terminal no-effect evidence for the I6 claim because O5 and D5 are unchanged.
fixture.reason: The idempotency identity is part of the provider proof domain. Rotating I5 to I6 can denote a distinct provider attempt namespace even when the logical operation and payload are unchanged. P_I5 therefore proves no-effect only for I5 and does not establish that no I6 attempt exists or can execute. Current repository fence freshness via F7 CAS/readback protects repository authority but cannot manufacture missing provider-side evidence for I6. Safe terminal negative closure for I6 requires an I6-scoped terminal proof or an independently verified equivalence/sealing invariant that explicitly proves I6 cannot introduce a new provider execution domain.

weak_rule_falsified.rule: If logical operation ID and payload digest are unchanged, a complete permanently sealed no-effect proof for an older provider idempotency identity can be reused for a later claim under a different provider idempotency identity without additional provider evidence.
weak_rule_falsified.falsification: I5 and I6 may be distinct provider execution domains. P_I5 seals only I5, so unchanged O5,D5 is insufficient to extend the proof to I6.

minimum_safe_conditions_for_cross_identi: An explicit provider-side invariant proves I5 and I6 map to the same immutable execution domain, or proves I6 cannot create/resume any provider attempt.
That invariant is itself exact-scope evidence covering O5,D5 and both identities.
The old proof remains complete and permanently sealed for the shared domain.
Current repository finalization still uses F7 CAS and exact readback.

observations: Operation identity, payload identity, provider idempotency identity, and repository claim epoch are separate safety dimensions.
A terminal proof can survive repository claim-epoch advancement when its provider domain is unchanged, but it does not automatically survive a provider idempotency-domain rotation.
Repository CAS freshness and provider terminal-evidence scope solve different problems and neither substitutes for the other.
inference: Within this exact fixture, P_I5 is out-of-scope for I6 unless a separately verified provider invariant collapses both identities into the same sealed execution domain. Therefore a recurring-Chat claim protocol must bind negative terminal evidence to the exact provider idempotency identity, or carry explicit cross-identity equivalence evidence, before accepting terminal no-effect closure after identity rotation.
